title: Recognising the T-plural
summary: Distinguish one item from more than one before building plural forms.
objectives: Distinguish a supplied singular and plural pair.
Connect the plural form with “more than one”.

sections.title: One or more than one
paragraphs: The basic singular names one item. The nominative T-plural commonly names more than one item when the noun is a plural subject.
This first step asks only whether a displayed form is singular or plural.

sections.title: The visible plural signal
paragraphs: In the stable forms used here, plural -t appears at the end.
Other Finnish plural cases are outside this pack.

steps: kynät names more than one pen.

commonMistakes: Do not treat every final t as a complete explanation of all Finnish plurals.
Do not add a second case ending.
Do not change a stable stem in this recognition step.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Is kirja singular or plural?
practiceExercises.explanation: kirja is singular. The singular is kirja (“book”); the T-plural is kirjat (“books”).

optionFeedback.singular: Correct. kirja is singular. The singular is kirja (“book”); the T-plural is kirjat (“books”).
optionFeedback.plural: kirja is not plural in this pair. kirja is singular. The singular is kirja (“book”); the T-plural is kirjat (“books”).
